questions.prompt: Put the stages of the engineering design process in order.
questions.explanation: Engineers define the problem, set constraints, brainstorm options, prototype a leading one, test it against the constraints, then iterate.

questions.prompt: In engineering, a solution that meets its constraints on time, budget, and safety is a legitimate stopping point even if it is not the only possible answer.
questions.explanation: Engineering aims at a working, safe, affordable solution within constraints, so good enough is a valid finish line.

questions.prompt: Match each engineering discipline to the question that dominates its problems.
pairs: How do forces move, support, or transform this object?
How does current, voltage, or a signal flow through this system?
Will this large structure stand safely for decades?
How do we run a reaction safely and profitably at industrial scale?
questions.explanation: Each discipline uses the same design process but focuses on a different kind of system.

questions.prompt: How many significant figures does the measurement 0.004200 have?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant, but the digits 4, 2 and the two trailing zeros after the decimal point are, giving 4.

questions.prompt: A calculator gives 4.2 × 3.14159 = 13.194678. How should the result be reported using significant figures?
questions.explanation: In multiplication the result keeps as many significant figures as the input with the fewest. 4.2 has 2, so the result is 13.

questions.prompt: A scale that reads 152.3 g, 152.4 g, and 152.2 g for an object whose true mass is 140 g is precise but not accurate.
questions.explanation: The readings cluster tightly (precise) but are far from the true value (not accurate).

questions.prompt: A 4 m beam rests on a support at each end. A 100 N weight sits 1 m from the left support. What force, in newtons, does the left support carry?
questions.explanation: Moments about the left support give the right support 100 x 1 / 4 = 25 N, and force balance leaves 100 - 25 = 75 N on the left.

questions.prompt: Which statements about trusses are true?
choices: Every member carries only tension or compression along its length
A triangle cannot change shape unless one of its sides changes length
The method of joints uses the two force equations (ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0) at each joint
The moment equation must be applied at every joint
A rectangle of hinged rods is rigid without any diagonal
answers: Every member carries only tension or compression along its length
A triangle cannot change shape unless one of its sides changes length
The method of joints uses the two force equations (ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0) at each joint
questions.explanation: Truss members carry axial force only, triangles are rigid, and forces at a pin all pass through one point, so only force equations apply. A hinged rectangle can collapse into a parallelogram.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a sketch of a single object, isolated from everything around it, with every force on it drawn as an arrow?
questions.explanation: A free-body diagram isolates one object so you can account for every force acting on it.

questions.prompt: Why is concrete, a brittle material, almost always paired with steel reinforcement?
choices: Steel is ductile and bends visibly before failing, giving advance warning
Steel is cheaper than concrete
Concrete cannot carry compression
Steel makes concrete lighter than aluminum
questions.answer: Steel is ductile and bends visibly before failing, giving advance warning
questions.explanation: Brittle materials fail suddenly; ductile steel deforms visibly first, warning of trouble.

questions.prompt: Fatigue can cause a part to fail under repeated loads that are each well below its yield point.
questions.explanation: Each cycle grows a microscopic crack, so enough repetitions break a part that a single load never would.

questions.prompt: Describe the "eliminate, then rank" method for choosing a material, and give one example of a hard requirement that eliminates a material.
rubric: Says to first remove materials that fail a hard requirement
Says to then rank the remaining materials on the criteria that matter most
Gives a valid hard-requirement example such as operating temperature above a polymer's melting point
Notes that no material is universally best, so the criteria depend on the application
questions.model: First eliminate any material that fails a hard requirement, for example a polymer that softens below an exhaust's operating temperature. Then rank the remaining materials on whichever criteria matter most for the job, such as cost, weight, and corrosion resistance. There is no universally best material; it depends on the application.
questions.explanation: Selection is a trade-off decision, so disqualify first and then weigh the remaining options.

questions.prompt: A constant 50 N force pushes a box 2 m along a floor in 4 seconds. What is the average power, in watts?
questions.explanation: Work is 50 x 2 = 100 J, and power is work divided by time: 100 / 4 = 25 W.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of negative feedback?
choices: A thermostat turning a heater off when the room gets too warm
A microphone picking up its own speaker's output and amplifying it
A battery draining while a phone is in use
A bridge deck twisting more as wind pushes it
questions.answer: A thermostat turning a heater off when the room gets too warm
questions.explanation: Negative feedback corrects deviation and pushes the system back toward a target.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: Pushes a system back toward a stable target
Amplifies deviation, pushing the system further away
Useful output divided by total input
Energy changes form but is never destroyed
questions.explanation: These are the core ideas of systems thinking and energy accounting.

questions.prompt: A 6 Ω resistor and a 3 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance, in ohms?
questions.explanation: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω, which is less than either resistor alone.

questions.prompt: In a series string of lights, one burned-out bulb breaks the only current path and turns off every bulb.
questions.explanation: A series circuit has a single loop, so an open anywhere stops current everywhere.

questions.prompt: Why do digital signals resist noise better than analog signals?
choices: The receiver only has to decide whether a value is closer to 0 or to 1
Digital signals carry no voltage
Noise cannot enter a digital wire
Digital signals vary continuously, so noise averages out
questions.answer: The receiver only has to decide whether a value is closer to 0 or to 1
questions.explanation: Moderate noise rarely changes which of two states is read, whereas any distortion directly corrupts an analog value.

questions.prompt: A cable fails at 12,000 N and is expected to carry at most 3,000 N. Using margin of safety = factor of safety - 1, what is the margin of safety (as a plain number, not a percentage)?
questions.explanation: FS = 12,000 / 3,000 = 4, so MS = 4 - 1 = 3, which is 300% extra capacity.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a code and a standard?
choices: A code is a legally enforceable set of minimum requirements; a standard is a detailed technical specification that a code often references
A code is voluntary; a standard is law
A code is written by individual engineers; a standard is written by juries
They mean the same thing
questions.answer: A code is a legally enforceable set of minimum requirements; a standard is a detailed technical specification that a code often references
questions.explanation: Governments adopt codes, while professional organizations such as ASME or IEEE write standards that codes can require.

questions.prompt: A client orders you to approve a design you know is unsafe. Explain why "the client told me to" is not an acceptable defense for an engineer.
rubric: States that public safety, health, and welfare come first
Says this obligation outranks duties to the client or employer
Says the engineer should refuse or escalate rather than comply
Mentions that a PE stamp is a personal, legal commitment
questions.model: Engineering ethics puts the safety, health, and welfare of the public first, ahead of any duty to a client or employer. The engineer must refuse or escalate instead of complying, because a PE stamp is a personal legal commitment, so blaming the client does not remove the engineer's responsibility.
questions.explanation: Engineering failures can harm people who had no say in the decision, so the public-first duty is enforced through licensure.

questions.prompt: Which best explains the 1940 Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapse?
choices: Wind-driven twisting formed a positive feedback loop that grew with each cycle
An earthquake shook the bridge apart
The bridge was overloaded by heavy traffic
A defective batch of steel snapped under normal load
questions.answer: Wind-driven twisting formed a positive feedback loop that grew with each cycle
questions.explanation: A steady 40 mph wind and the deck's twisting reinforced each other until the structure failed; there was no earthquake, overload, or material defect.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of the footbridge design walkthrough in the order the capstone presents them.
items: Apply a factor of safety and codes
Consider the whole system, such as wind-driven effects
Take responsibility for ethics and public safety
questions.explanation: The capstone walks from defining the brief through analysis and margin, then whole-system checks, and finishes with ethical responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which of these are connected to the Tacoma Narrows collapse in the case study?
choices: A positive feedback loop between twisting and wind forces
Alternating wind forces matching a natural twisting mode of the structure
A design focus on static loads with little attention to dynamic wind behavior
A defect in the steel material
Overloading from heavy traffic
answers: A positive feedback loop between twisting and wind forces
Alternating wind forces matching a natural twisting mode of the structure
A design focus on static loads with little attention to dynamic wind behavior
questions.explanation: The collapse came from dynamic wind effects and a design process that had not yet accounted for them, not from material defects or overloading.
